chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abu Harun al-Makfuf, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Harun! The Iqamah is part of the Salat. So when you establish it, do not speak, nor gesture with your hand.'

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: Iqamah: The second call to prayer, recited immediately before the prayer begins.
key_terms.تُومِ: Tum: To gesture or signal with the hand.

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette regarding speech and gestures during the Iqamah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual gravity of the Iqamah by instructing Abu Harun al-Makfuf to remain silent and refrain from hand gestures during its recitation. This directive highlights the Iqamah not merely as a procedural announcement but as a moment of reverent preparation, aligning the worshipper’s physical stillness with the internal focus required for the prayer. Such attention to detail reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adab (etiquette) and khushu (devotion) in transitioning from the call to the actual act of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Abu Haroun Al Makfouf who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘O Abu Haroun! The Iqamah is from the Salāt. So when you establish it, so neither speak nor gesture with your hands’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Salih ibn ‘Uqbah from abu Harun al-Makfuf who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘O abu Harun, ‘Iqamah is part of Salah (prayer). When you say it do not speak or point with your hands.’”
